messages:
Wei Chen: quickstart updates for usage insights: what’s the *minimal* snippet we want to include to teach route tagging? trying to avoid a whole section but also don’t want people to end up with `Unknown route` everywhere.

Elliot Price: +1. I’m updating the quickstart + docs page this week. If we can standardize on one way across SDKs (param vs header) that’d be ideal. Also how do we show naming for common frameworks without going deep on every framework.

Monica Patel: current SDK direction:
- TS: `route` option on request helpers (maps to header)
- Python: `route=` kwarg (also maps to header)
- Go: TBD but likely same header + helper
So in quickstart we can show `route: "quickstart.chat"` / `route="quickstart.chat"` and add a short note “use stable, low-cardinality names”.

Alex Martinez: keep it to like 6-10 lines max in the quickstart. If we want frameworks, do it as *one* paragraph + examples (Express/FastAPI) in the docs page, and link from quickstart.

Paula Mendes: from product POV: the single most important thing is they don’t pass raw URL paths with IDs. We should call it out explicitly (“don’t use `/users/123`”).

Tessa Morgan: can we use wording like “Route = logical endpoint name” and show a couple formats? e.g. `billing.create_invoice` vs `chat.generate`.

Wei Chen: ok. proposing quickstart snippet includes:
1) client init
2) one request with `route` set
3) comment line about “stable string; no user ids”
And then link to full route naming section.

Monica Patel: for TS quickstart, something like:
```ts
import { Redwood } from "@redwood-ai/sdk";

const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY! });

const res = await client.responses.create({
  model: "redwood/llama-3.1-70b",
  input: "Write a support reply...",
  route: "support.reply.generate", // stable name; avoid user IDs / request paths
});
```
We can swap endpoint name if quickstart is chat-based, but gist is that.

Elliot Price: looks good. For Python equivalent:
```py
from redwood import Redwood

client = Redwood()

resp = client.responses.create(
  model="redwood/llama-3.1-70b",
  input="Write a support reply...",
  route="support.reply.generate",  # stable; avoid user IDs / raw URLs
)
```
Then docs page can have the longer “frameworks” section.

Dylan Brooks: what about streaming quickstart? does `route` work on stream path too?

Monica Patel: yes, route is part of request object and should be included for streaming the same way. If the quickstart uses streaming we can keep it the same, just swap the call to `.stream(...)` and keep `route` in the payload.

Paula Mendes: + please add a sentence that if they *don’t* set it, we’ll show `Unknown route` and it’ll group everything together. That’s the common support ticket.

Wei Chen: framework guidance (docs) — minimal examples I’m thinking:
- Express: set route string based on handler (not `req.path`)
- FastAPI: use `request.scope["route"].name` or a constant per endpoint
- Next.js: use the route segment name, not the full URL
Anything else we should call out?

Alex Martinez: avoid telling people to use raw OpenTelemetry route attribute unless we’re sure it matches our normalization rules. Keep it simple: “pick a stable string per endpoint; use the route template if you must.”

Tessa Morgan: we should show an example of the “templated path” style too, since people will ask:
- good: `POST /v1/chat/completions`
- ok: `POST /users/:id/messages` (template)
- bad: `POST /users/123/messages`

Monica Patel: agree. Also note about length/characters? (whatever we decided: lower-ish cardinality, <= 80 chars, limited charset). But we can just say “short” in quickstart and link to naming doc for specifics.

Elliot Price: I’ll add a “Route naming conventions” section with:
- recommended formats: `service.action`, `team.product.endpoint`
- allowed chars (keep to `[a-zA-Z0-9._/-]` in examples)
- explicit “do not include dynamic IDs” callout
- 2 small framework snippets

Wei Chen: can we include one “middleware” example for Express? something like:
```ts
app.post("/v1/summarize", async (req, res) => {
  const route = "summarize.create";
  await client.responses.create({ model, input, route });
  ...
});
```

Monica Patel: yep. For FastAPI:
```py
@app.post("/v1/summarize", name="summarize.create")
async def summarize(request: Request):
    route = request.scope.get("route").name or "summarize.create"
    client.responses.create(..., route=route)
```
(We can simplify to constant if we don’t want to mention scope.)

Dylan Brooks: +1 to constant per handler. Mentioning scope might confuse folks.

Paula Mendes: decision from PM side: constant per endpoint is fine. We can say “if your framework supports route templates/names, use those.”

Wei Chen: ok, action items:
- Elliot: update quickstart with 1 request showing `route`, add link to docs section
- Monica: confirm exact property name across TS/Py in latest SDKs so we don’t ship docs that don’t compile
- Wei: draft framework examples (Express + FastAPI) and “good/bad” naming callout

Elliot Price: :thumbsup: I’ll push a PR today and ping for review.

Monica Patel: I’ll sanity check against the TS SDK PR + Python branch and reply here with exact names (I think it’s `route` everywhere, but want to confirm).

Tessa Morgan: once you have the final text, send me the quickstart excerpt. I’ll make sure wording matches console UI (“Route” vs “Endpoint”).

Wei Chen: will do. thanks all.
